bib.title: ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge

question: How was the ILSVRC benchmark built and evaluated, what progress in large-scale object recognition did it enable over 2010-2014, and how does the best computer vision compare with humans?
contributions: Discuss the challenges of creating this large-scale object recognition benchmark dataset
Highlight the developments in object classification and detection that resulted
Take a closer look at the current state of categorical object recognition (incl. human comparison)

method.summary: Describes the ILSVRC dataset construction (WordNet-based categories, search-engine candidates, AMT verification, a three-step bounding box pipeline, hierarchical multi-label annotation for detection), the evaluation metrics, a survey of 2010-2014 entries, bootstrap significance tests, per-class analysis of an 'optimistic' best-of-all-entries model, and a human vs GoogLeNet study with two annotators.

inference.samples: Evaluated entries are submitted by participants; bootstrap rounds from 20,000 until convergence; human study 1500 images (A1), 258 (A2)

metrics.name: top-5 classification error
metrics.definition: error = 1/N sum_i min_j d_ij; d=1 if predicted label != ground truth; 5 labels allowed

metrics.name: top-1 error and hierarchical error
metrics.definition: top-1 uses highest-confidence label; hierarchical cost = height of lowest common ancestor in ImageNet hierarchy; produced the same ordering, so only top-5 used since 2012

metrics.name: single-object localization error
metrics.definition: d_ij = max(label error, min_k box error); box error 0 if IOU>0.5 else 1; top-5

metrics.name: detection AP / mAP
metrics.definition: Greedy matching of detections to ground truth by descending confidence; AP over recall levels per class; winner = most classes won; mAP reported

metrics.name: chance performance of localization (CPL) and clutter
metrics.definition: CPL=sum_i sum_{j!=i} 1[IOU(Bi,Bj)>=0.5] / N(N-1); Clutter=log2(mean number of objectness windows before localizing target)

eval.protocol: Participants submit predictions to a server; test annotations hidden; 99.9% bootstrap CIs (20,000+ rounds) for entries; 95% bootstrap CI over classes for property analysis with scale normalisation; z-test for human vs GoogLeNet (one-sided p=0.022). Challenge deadline about 4 months after data release.

limits: Authors concede the dataset has one label per image in classification, creating ambiguity, handled by top-5.
Remaining annotation errors come mostly from fine-grained classes since crowd labelers are non-expert.
Detection 2013 vs 2014 numbers are not directly comparable: training set grew and 2014 winner used external data.
Human study has only two annotators; A2 trained on 100 images and labelled 258; humans needed heavy training.
Categories changed 2010->11->12, so cross-year comparison relies on constant scale.
Rules on outside data were first revised in 2014; authors expect further revision.
Does not report training compute, hyperparameters or seeds of entries; those are participants' own.
